visual_grammar.background: full-bleed dark graphite to ceramic-black gradient with a subtle matte industrial texture, faint vignetting at the edges, and occasional low-contrast thermal-vector field overlays in cyan-to-deep-orange used only as restrained background structure
visual_grammar.foreground: warm off-white engineering text and pale gray diagram strokes with high contrast against the dark field, never pure white, optimized for precise technical readability
visual_grammar.accent: copper-trace metallic accent paired with selective cyan thermal-route highlights; copper is the primary material accent and cyan is reserved for active paths, sensor readouts, and control emphasis
visual_grammar.typography: precise neo-grotesk sans for headlines and body, medium-to-bold uppercase section labels, large bold sentence-case headlines, compact regular body copy, and monospace micro-annotations for dimensions, control intervals, and system labels
visual_grammar.diagram_style: semiconductor-launch technical diagrams with thin orthographic outlines, directional thermal arrows, hex-cell lattice motifs, topological routing overlays, minimal fills, and controlled use of cyan-to-orange heat gradients only inside thermal maps or flow paths
visual_grammar.panel_style: charcoal translucent panels and callout cards with soft inner shadow, faint ceramic-gray borders, rounded corners kept minimal, and occasional copper keylines for product-boundary or system-architecture emphasis
visual_grammar.grid_system: 12-column grid with wide outer margins, strong left-aligned header band, disciplined baseline spacing, frequent split layouts of 5/7 or 4/8 columns, and centered hero-object compositions when the slide is product-led
visual_grammar.line_weight: fine engineering hairlines around 1 to 1.5 px for dividers and annotations, with slightly heavier 2 px strokes for key routes, boundaries, and emphasis frames

storyboard.title: Vitriflux
storyboard.purpose: Title / hero cover. Establish the company and product category with a single dominant object and a short tagline. No argument yet. Speaker notes should frame Vitriflux as a software-defined thermal backplane for AI hardware and signal that the category shift is from passive cooling geometry to addressable thermal routing.
storyboard.image_prompt: Create a clean full-bleed digital screenshot of a single presentation slide, edge-to-edge, no software UI, no browser chrome, no presenter view, no speaker notes visible, no page number, no slide count, and no pagination indicator anywhere. This is the one and only title cover slide. Use a dominant centered hero composition based on the user-provided concept representation: a thin black rectangular ceramic thermal-routing plate with a subtle hexagonal cell lattice, copper-toned traces near one edge, and industrial fluid connectors, rendered as a polished concept product image rather than a photographed prototype. Place the product large and slightly angled on a dark field with generous negative space. Add the company name 'Vitriflux' prominently and one short tagline beneath it: 'A software-defined thermal backplane for AI hardware.' Include no diagrams, no charts, no multi-panel layout, and no dense text. Optionally include a faint distant monitor-like thermal map glow in the background to imply thermal routing, but keep the plate as the clear focal object.

storyboard.title: Cooling is still built for a static map. AI heat is not.
storyboard.purpose: Open the argument with the core mismatch. Present today’s cooling assumption versus actual workload-shaped heat behavior. This slide should make the audience feel the category error before introducing Vitriflux as the solution.
storyboard.image_prompt: Create a clean full-bleed digital screenshot of a single presentation slide, edge-to-edge, no application chrome or UI, no page number, slide count, or pagination indicator anywhere. Build a two-panel contrast layout. Left side: a simplified board or tray graphic under the heading 'Static cooling assumption' showing a fixed worst-case thermal map with uniform local cooling zones, rigid plumbing lines, and overprovisioned capacity illustrated as broad passive channels. Right side: a dynamic thermal field under the heading 'Actual AI heat behavior' showing moving hotspots across chips, boards, and rack-level paths with several different hotspot positions and directional movement overlays. Use minimal text blocks with short phrases only, such as 'designed around local worst case' on the left and 'hotspots move with workload placement' on the right. The visual should frame heat like traffic, with congestion, rerouting, and finite sink capacity, not as a generic red cloud. Keep the slide argument-led, not product-led.

storyboard.title: Static cooling wastes capacity to protect against moving hotspots.
storyboard.purpose: Translate the mismatch into operational pain. Show why fixed plumbing forces oversized pumps, aggressive coolant temperatures, redundant manifolds, and unused cooling headroom. This is the bridge from technical problem to economic importance.
storyboard.image_prompt: Create a clean full-bleed digital screenshot of a single presentation slide, no software interface elements, no page number, no slide count, no pagination indicator. Use a left-right layout. On the left, show a stylized liquid-cooled accelerator tray or rack thermal diagram with several chips or modules producing uneven heat while fixed coolant paths remain unchanged. Overlay zones of stranded capacity and localized thermal congestion. On the right, stack four concise callout cards with iconography and short labels derived from the source material: 'Oversized pumps', 'Aggressive coolant temperatures', 'Redundant manifolds', and 'Unused cooling capacity'. Add one small concluding statement at the bottom right: 'Static worst-case design trades efficiency for insurance.' Keep all visuals conceptual and schematic; do not imply measured results or real deployments.

storyboard.title: Vitriflux adds an addressable thermal-routing layer.
storyboard.purpose: Introduce the invention clearly and precisely. Present the plate as a backplane or switch fabric between variable heat sources and existing cooling interfaces. This is the mental-model slide.
storyboard.image_prompt: Create a clean full-bleed digital screenshot of a single presentation slide, edge-to-edge, no UI, no page number, no pagination. Use a centered layered system diagram. Top layer: several accelerator modules or heat sources. Middle layer: a large Vitriflux plate rendered as a black ceramic slab with a subtle hexagonal cell grid and copper trace accents, labeled 'Field-addressable ceramic thermal-routing plate'. Bottom or side layer: two to four coolant interfaces feeding into an existing liquid loop. Overlay directional thermal paths moving from hotspots through the plate toward whichever cooling interface has capacity. Include a concise side annotation that says, in substance, 'Routes heat through hardware the way a network switch routes data.' The slide should visually establish the plate as an addressable layer, not as a pump, chiller, or facility replacement.

storyboard.title: What the system does — and what it does not do
storyboard.purpose: Build trust through boundary discipline. Explicitly separate redistribution from removal and list the product boundary from the source document. This slide defuses skepticism.
storyboard.image_prompt: Create a clean full-bleed digital screenshot of a single presentation slide with no application UI and absolutely no page number or pagination marker. Use a strong two-column layout with a vertical divider. Left column heading: 'Does'. Present five concise bullets from the source intent: redistributes heat across high-power assemblies before transfer into liquid cooling; senses spatial temperature field; routes heat toward available cooling interfaces; balances load between coolant interfaces; intended to reduce transient peaks and throttling. Right column heading: 'Does not'. Present the product-boundary items from the source: refrigerate the coolant; eliminate pumps or facility heat rejection; change semiconductor junction design; replace all local thermal-interface materials; guarantee improved performance before cell-level switching is validated. Add a small bottom note: 'The product redistributes heat; existing infrastructure still removes it.' Keep the slide clean, precise, and non-defensive.

storyboard.title: How thermal routing could work at the cell level
storyboard.purpose: Present the proposed operating principle without overstating certainty. Show the cell anatomy and note that the exact physics has not yet been selected. This is where scientific seriousness becomes visible.
storyboard.image_prompt: Create a clean full-bleed digital screenshot of a single slide, no software chrome, no page number, no slide count, no pagination indicator. Use a large cutaway technical illustration of one or several thermal-routing cells inside the plate. Label the source-backed components: high-conductivity ceramic body, addressable electrode structure, anisotropic thermal path, local temperature sensing, and electrical/thermal connection to adjacent cells. Include a surrounding mini-grid to show how coordinated cells create preferential paths. Add a clearly separated note box titled 'Working hypothesis' that states, in concise source-faithful language, that an applied field may alter the cell’s effective thermal-conductivity tensor through ferroic domain control, interfacial switching, or another field-responsive solid-state mechanism. Add a small caution line: 'Exact cell physics not yet selected; candidate mechanisms require comparative testing.' The slide must feel rigorous and exploratory, not validated.

storyboard.title: System architecture
storyboard.purpose: Translate the concept into a complete stack that engineers and partners can diligence. Show the components and control loop from sensor input to routing state to coolant interfaces.
storyboard.image_prompt: Create a clean full-bleed digital screenshot of a single presentation slide, no app UI, no page number or pagination. Build a horizontal architecture diagram with six clearly labeled blocks from the source document: Ceramic routing plate, Thermal-cell array, Sensor layer, Edge controller, Host interface, Control software, and include Coolant interfaces as the heat transfer endpoint in the system. Show arrows for both thermal flow and control/data flow, visually distinguished. Include a small note beneath Host interface: 'accepts workload or board telemetry when available.' Include another note beneath the controller path: 'first control system does not require predictive workload scheduling.' This should read like an infrastructure control-plane diagram, not a consumer infographic.

storyboard.title: First product: designed to fit existing liquid-cooled AI hardware
storyboard.purpose: Make the entry wedge credible. Show integration location, first-product envelope, and serviceability. This is the slide that converts hardware skeptics.
storyboard.image_prompt: Create a clean full-bleed digital screenshot of a single slide with no software chrome and no page number, slide count, or pagination indicator. Use a large exploded integration view of an accelerator assembly: accelerator modules above, Vitriflux plate in the middle, and existing liquid-cooling loop / manifold interfaces below or to the side. The plate should mount between the accelerator assembly and two or more coolant manifolds. Add a disciplined specifications panel using source-backed development targets labeled clearly as 'Development targets, not validated specifications'. Include: plate footprint approximately 500 × 350 mm; plate thickness less than 12 mm; thermal zones 256–1,024 addressable cells; coolant interfaces 2–4; control interval below 100 ms; added electrical load below 2% of managed thermal load; integration with existing accelerator tray and coolant loop; serviceability replaceable field module; design life five years continuous operation. Present these as crisp engineering targets, not proven specs.

storyboard.title: Why this matters economically
storyboard.purpose: Tie technical performance to infrastructure value without inventing outcomes. Show the economic logic buyers care about: density, throttling, overprovisioning, and cooling-power efficiency.
storyboard.image_prompt: Create a clean full-bleed digital screenshot of a single presentation slide, full-bleed, no UI, no page number, no pagination. Use a left column with a simple cause-and-effect chain diagram starting from 'Dynamic thermal field' to 'Static cooling overprovisions locally' to 'Capital and power inefficiency'. On the right, create four larger value cards derived from the source value proposition: 'More compute per rack', 'Fewer throttling events', 'Less worst-case overprovisioning', and 'Improved use of redundant cooling paths'. Add a fifth smaller card or footer statement: 'Greater tolerance for uneven hardware loads'. Keep wording prospective and qualitative; do not include numerical ROI claims or performance figures.

storyboard.title: Commercialization: start where pain is sharp and integration is lowest-friction
storyboard.purpose: Provide the required commercialization strategy. Show who buys, who uses, the adoption wedge, partner path, revenue mechanism, and how the company scales without inventing traction or pricing.
storyboard.image_prompt: Create a clean full-bleed digital screenshot of a single presentation slide with no application chrome and no page number or pagination indicator anywhere. Use a structured 2x2 layout plus a bottom strip. Top left quadrant: 'Who buys / who uses' with two rows: Primary user — Data-center thermal or hardware operations team; Economic buyer — AI infrastructure operator or accelerator-system manufacturer. Top right quadrant: 'Adoption wedge' showing initial application in a liquid-cooled AI accelerator assembly containing multiple high-power processors with workload-varying thermal loads, and a first insertion point between accelerator assembly and existing liquid loop. Bottom left quadrant: 'Integration path' listing Server OEM, cold-plate manufacturer, or liquid-cooling provider as integration partners, visualized as a staged path from evaluation to joint development to OEM pilot to production integration. Bottom right quadrant: 'Revenue mechanism' using only source-backed structure: initial revenue would come from paid evaluation units and joint-development programs; production revenue could use per-plate hardware sales, control-software licensing, OEM integration agreements, and performance monitoring / fleet optimization. Bottom full-width strip: 'Scale logic' showing that the company should avoid overcommitting to recurring software revenue until the hardware creates a persistent operational dataset customers will pay to use. Keep the slide explicit, credible, and free of invented customers or prices.

storyboard.title: Development program and evidence gates
storyboard.purpose: Show that uncertainty is decomposed into a disciplined program. This slide should turn scientific and engineering risk into diligence structure.
storyboard.image_prompt: Create a clean full-bleed digital screenshot of a single presentation slide, no software UI, no page number, no pagination. Build a four-phase horizontal roadmap with compact technical icons and clear pass conditions. Phase 1 — Cell validation: fabricate small ceramic coupons and measure whether candidate field-responsive structures produce a repeatable change in magnitude or direction of thermal transport; pass condition: reversible, measurable modulation large enough to affect a modeled multi-source thermal field. Phase 2 — Array demonstrator: construct a small addressable grid beneath several independently controlled heaters; pass condition: lower peak temperature than an equivalent passive plate under the same total heat load and sink capacity. Phase 3 — Accelerator emulator: integrate a full plate with a liquid loop and a programmable multi-zone heater representing an AI board; pass condition: demonstrate hotspot redistribution, reduced throttling-equivalent exposure, and acceptable control power. Phase 4 — OEM pilot: package the plate for an existing accelerator tray and evaluate it with a cooling or server partner. Make all evidence formats schematic, not actual results.

storyboard.title: Principal uncertainties the company is already designed to answer
storyboard.purpose: Address the obvious diligence questions directly. This slide should project seriousness by naming the risks rather than hiding them.
storyboard.image_prompt: Create a clean full-bleed digital screenshot of a single slide with no UI and no page number, slide count, or pagination indicator. Use a matrix or stacked-card layout titled 'Principal uncertainties'. Include the exact source-backed themes as concise risk cards: whether field-responsive ceramic structures provide sufficient thermal modulation; switching speed at useful plate thickness; thermal resistance introduced by electrodes and interfaces; manufacturing yield across a large multilayer plate; failure behavior under continuous thermal cycling; whether performance gain exceeds integration cost; whether server OEMs prefer direct integration over a retrofit module. Add a narrow right-side column titled 'What evaluation must show' with abstract check marks for physics viability, integration viability, and economic viability. Do not imply these have been satisfied.

storyboard.title: Why AI infrastructure first — and where the platform can extend
storyboard.purpose: Earn the platform story by showing that AI is the urgent wedge and adjacent markets are a consequence of the architecture, not current business sprawl.
storyboard.image_prompt: Create a clean full-bleed digital screenshot of a single presentation slide, no application chrome, no page number or pagination indicator. Use a left-to-right expansion graphic. Left side: a large primary tile labeled 'AI infrastructure' with supporting phrases like 'immediate value for every recovered watt and square centimeter' and 'liquid-cooled accelerator assemblies'. To the right, show four smaller adjacent opportunity tiles connected by a controlled expansion line: power electronics, battery systems, aerospace electronics, and industrial equipment with irregular thermal loads. Include a small framing note: 'Strategic horizon after initial product validation.' Make the slide visually clear that AI infrastructure is first and current, while adjacencies are later platform applications.

storyboard.title: The thermal control plane for dense compute
storyboard.purpose: Close with the category claim, the narrow initial product, and the invitation to engage in diligence or partnership. This final slide should feel inevitable, not inflated.
storyboard.image_prompt: Create a clean full-bleed digital screenshot of a single presentation slide with no software UI and no page number, slide count, or pagination anywhere. Use a strong closing composition with the Vitriflux plate centered or slightly offset, overlaid by a simplified thermal-routing network map connecting moving hotspots to multiple cooling interfaces. On the left or top, place a concise three-line close: 'Addressable thermal management, not passive plumbing.' 'A credible first product for existing liquid-cooled AI hardware.' 'A platform architecture spanning hardware, control, and data.' On the opposite side, add a restrained callout block titled 'Engagement path' with short lines such as 'technical diligence', 'joint development', and 'OEM / cooling-partner evaluation' without implying any existing commitments. The overall impression should be that a new system layer has been named clearly and can now be evaluated seriously.
